headline: Bitcoin held above 81,000 dollars through the weekend after the CFTC sent crypto market structure rules to the White House, a move that had already lifted Strategy 16.4 percent and Coinbase 11.7 percent on Friday while the US 10 year Treasury yield closed the week back at 5 percent.

summary.us: The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,650.50, up 0.17 percent, and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.39 percent to 26,522.55, while the Dow slipped about 0.2 percent to 51,682.64 and the 10 year Treasury yield returned to 5.004 percent. The moves followed the Federal Reserve's 25 basis point hike on 16 September to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first increase in three years, after which Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation is too high and futures moved to price a 58 percent chance of another hike in October.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 rose 0.33 percent on Friday to 23,346.40 and Bank Nifty gained 0.54 percent to 56,358.70, but the Sensex ended flat at 74,294.96 and both benchmarks logged a sixth consecutive weekly loss, the longest run since 2020, under crude above 100 dollars and liquidity drained by the 22,562 crore rupee NSE IPO. The Tata Sons and Tata Trusts governance dispute knocked TCS down 3.88 percent while Jefferies buy ratings lifted the Adani complex, FIIs bought a net 599.50 crore rupees and DIIs a net 1,019.70 crore rupees in the cash segment, and the rupee sat near 95.9 per dollar.
summary.global: Asia closed higher, with the Nikkei 225 up 1.38 percent to 65,018.95 after the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.25 percent on a split vote that sent the yen past 156 per dollar, the KOSPI up 2.66 percent on an AI memory chip rally led by Samsung and SK hynix, and the Hang Seng up 0.60 percent. Europe went the other way as the STOXX 600 fell 1.1 percent, the FTSE 100 lost 1.45 percent and the DAX 1.60 percent, dragged by a 3.4 percent slide in autos after Volkswagen cut its outlook and flagged 10 billion euros of one off items.

calendar.what: Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee speaks and the Chicago Fed National Activity Index is released, opening a week with about ten Fed speaker appearances. The NSE and Sonaselection India IPOs close in India.

Richmond Fed manufacturing index for September at 10:00 US Eastern. AutoZone, MillerKnoll and Thor Industries report before the US open, KB Home and Worthington after the close. Varmora Granito IPO opens in India. The Avalanche Helicon upgrade activates at 15:00 UTC.

S&P Global flash US manufacturing and services PMIs for September, plus the US current account. Swastika Infra, ArMee Infotech and Elevate Campuses IPOs open in India. Bamboo Insurance and Amaero are set to price in the US.
MBA mortgage applications and US new home sales. A-One Steels India IPO opens. BW Industrial Holdings and Web3Labs Global are on the US pricing calendar.

US initial jobless claims, durable goods orders and the final reading of second quarter GDP. The Swastika Infra, ArMee Infotech and Elevate Campuses IPOs close in India. The August PCE price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, is the next major US release after this.
No scheduled market events. Markets are closed for the weekend.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to central banks. The Federal Reserve raised rates a quarter point on 16 September to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first hike since 2023, and the Bank of Japan followed on 18 September with a split 7 to 2 vote that lifted its policy rate to a 31 year high of 1.25 percent, yet the yen weakened past 156 per dollar because two board members dissented and Governor Ueda made no commitment to further moves. US equities finished mixed as the 10 year Treasury yield came back to about 5 percent after touching a 19 year high above 5.04 percent ahead of the Fed, with the Dow down 1.69 percent on the week while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.72 percent. India was the weak spot, where the Nifty and Sensex logged a sixth consecutive weekly decline, the longest losing run in six years, under crude above 100 dollars, tighter global policy and a deepening Tata Sons governance dispute. Metals held their ground, with copper up about 2 percent on the week as the Yangshan import premium climbed 72 percent in September to a near four year high and silver adding 3.46 percent, while crypto turned sharply higher into the weekend on post Fed relief and rotation into altcoins. Next week brings S&P Global flash PMIs on 23 September, a heavy run of Fed speakers, Costco and Nike earnings on 24 September, and in India the Varmora Granito, Elevate Campuses, ArMee Infotech and A-One Steels offers alongside the close of the NSE IPO on 21 September.
